title: rubus rhombifolius subsp. castellarnaui
intro: Rubus rhombifolius subsp. castellarnaui, commonly known as Castilian blackberry, is a lesser-known subspecies of the blackberry plant genus Rubus. It is a shrub native to the Iberian Peninsula in Europe, characterized by its dark purple fruit and thorny stems. The Castilian blackberry has been traditionally used for its health benefits, particularly in treating digestive issues and skin problems, due to its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. The plant contains bioactive constituents such as ellagic acid, anthocyanins, and flavonoids, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, including antimicrobial, antiproliferative, and anti-inflammatory effects.
